newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian trains collide, at least 12 dead.
newsitem.headline: Indian trains collide, at least 12 dead.

text.p: At least 12 people died and about 80 were injured when one passenger train smashed into another early on Monday near the Indian capital New Delhi, officials and eyewitnesses said.

"We can confirm 12 people died in the accident," M.S. Ahlawat, a deputy superintendent of police, told Reuters at the crash site. "About four or five more seriously injured people may not survive." A railway police official, Deepa Mehta, had earlier put the death toll at 15.
K.K. Gupta, a senior railway manager in charge of rescue operations, said the speeding Karnataka Express had overshot a stop signal on a loop line and rammed into the slower-moving Himsagar Express.
"There are many people with minor injuries but at least 40 are seriously injured," Gupta said.
Rescuers looking for bodies or survivors were working in pre-dawn darkness to cut through the mangled metal of at least eight coaches that were thrown off the tracks by the impact.

I.K. Joseph, a survivor travelling on the Himsagar Express, said: "There was a big bang. I was sleeping on the top berth and I fell down and the lights went off. When I lit a match the coach had overturned and I crawled out of a window."
